rules.title: Conductor ampacity
rules.summary: The current a conductor may carry, read from the ampacity table in the column its terminals allow: #3/0 copper carries 200 A at 75 °C, which is why a 200 A feeder is #3/0.

values.when: #3/0 copper THHN, read in the 75 °C terminal column

rules.title: Conduit fill limits
rules.summary: How much of a raceway's inside area conductors may fill — 53% for one, 31% for two, 40% for three or more.

rules.title: Disconnect within sight of the unit
rules.summary: Air-conditioning and refrigeration equipment gets a disconnect within sight of it and readily reached, so the rooftop unit's circuit ends in a disconnect on the roof.

values.when: air-conditioning or refrigerating equipment, the rooftop unit
values.value: a disconnect within sight of the unit, readily accessible

rules.title: Means of egress illumination on emergency power
rules.summary: The building code's side of the exit lights: the path out stays lit on emergency power for 90 minutes when the normal power fails.

values.when: egress path lighting on emergency power, light with the power out

rules.title: Grounding electrode conductor size
rules.summary: The conductor from the service to the water pipe and the ground rods is sized from the service conductors, and #3/0 copper service conductors want a #4 copper grounding electrode conductor.

values.when: copper service conductors #2/0 or #3/0, copper electrode conductor

rules.title: Emergency lighting battery duration
rules.summary: How long an emergency lighting source must carry its load with the normal power out, 90 minutes, which is why every exit sign and emergency light on a small job carries a battery.

values.when: emergency lighting and exit signs, light with the power out (battery unit equipment)

rules.title: EMT bends between pull points
rules.summary: A run of EMT may turn no more than 360° in total between pull points, the equal of four quarter bends, so a run with more needs a box or conduit body in it.

values.when: total of the bends in one run, box to box or pull point to pull point

rules.title: EMT support spacing
rules.summary: Where EMT is strapped, within 3 ft of every box or termination and at least every 10 ft along the run, which is the strap count on a takeoff.

values.when: from each box or other termination

rules.title: Equipment grounding conductor size
rules.summary: The ground that rides with a feeder is sized from the breaker ahead of it, not from the phase wires, and a 200 A breaker wants a #6 copper ground.

rules.title: Circuits for fixed equipment
rules.summary: The code limits what may share a branch circuit with equipment fastened in place, and the simple way to live within it is a circuit each, as the restaurant gives its dishwasher, pump and rooftop unit.

values.when: equipment fastened in place, on a 15 or 20 A circuit that also feeds lights or plug-in loads
values.value: no more than half the circuit's rating

rules.title: GFCI protection, non-dwelling
rules.summary: Where a commercial building's receptacles must be ground-fault protected, as the course counts them in a restaurant (restrooms, kitchens, food and beverage areas with a sink, within 6 ft of a sink), and the dishwasher's own GFCI.

values.when: areas with a sink and food or beverage preparation or cooking, 210.8(B)(3) in 2023 (part of (B)(2) in 2020)
near a sink, from the top inside edge of the bowl, 210.8(B)(7) in 2023 ((B)(5) in 2017 and 2020)
a dishwasher, 150 V or less to ground and 60 A or less, 422.5(A)(7), 2020 on

rules.title: Shunt trip on hood suppression
rules.summary: When a kitchen hood's fire-suppression system fires, the electric power to the cooking equipment under it shuts off by itself, usually through a shunt-trip breaker wired to the system.

values.value: power to the cooking equipment under the hood shuts off automatically

rules.title: Make-up on a vertical
rules.summary: The foot of conduit the app adds to every vertical it writes, for the box entry and the bend that plan view never shows.

values.when: every device vertical the Chain tool writes

source.section: estimating convention; not a code figure

rules.title: Default mount heights for devices
rules.summary: The heights above finished floor the app starts each device at — 18" receptacles, 44" GFCI at a counter, 48" switches, 78" panel top — so the Chain tool can write the vertical.

rules.title: Occupant sensor lighting controls
rules.summary: The energy code wants the lights in rooms people leave, restrooms, storage and break rooms among them, on sensors that turn them off by themselves, and every other area on a time switch.

values.when: restrooms, storage rooms, break rooms and the other spaces the section lists (2021 adds corridors; enclosed spaces of 300 sq ft or less are listed)
values.value: an occupant sensor that turns the lights off

values.when: every other area, not on occupant sensors (C405.2.2)
values.value: time-switch control that turns the lights off on a schedule

rules.title: Service and feeder load calculation
rules.summary: A service or feeder is sized by the engineer's load calculation under Article 220 (for a new restaurant, the optional method of 220.88), never less than the calculated load, and in practice with room for what the owner adds later.

values.value: rated for at least the load Article 220 calculates

values.when: a new restaurant, not all electric, 200 kVA or less connected, by the optional method (220.88)

rules.title: Small conductor protection
rules.summary: The largest breaker the code lets protect the small copper sizes, 15 A on #14, 20 A on #12 and 30 A on #10, which is why a 20 A circuit is #12.

rules.title: The K constant for voltage drop
rules.summary: The resistivity figure the estimator's single-phase voltage-drop formula uses — 12.9 for copper, 21.2 for aluminum, in ohm-circular-mils per foot.

source.section: Chapter 9, Table 8 (as the trade rounds it)

rules.title: Voltage drop on a branch circuit
rules.summary: The app flags a branch circuit whose drop to the farthest device exceeds 3% — the NEC's informational recommendation, not a requirement.

values.when: branch circuit, to the farthest device

rules.title: Working space clearance
rules.summary: The clear space the code keeps in front of a panel someone may work on live, as the course teaches it at 120/208 V: 36 in deep from the panel's face, 30 in wide, 6 ft 6 in high.

values.when: depth, clear in front of the enclosure (0 to 150 V to ground, any condition)
width, or the equipment's own width if that is wider
height, from the floor, or the equipment's own height if that is taller

rules.title: Diffuser neck velocity
rules.summary: A diffuser's neck is picked from the maker's sound and throw data and the push its flex needs; makers keep neck velocity under about 1,000 feet a minute, and the app's own neck suggestion puts up to 150 CFM on an 8 in neck and up to 300 on a 10 in, so the neck size is the flex and tap size on the bid.

values.when: a common ceiling for air through a supply diffuser's neck (makers' selection guidance)
150 CFM through an 8 in neck (the neck-size suggestion's first row)
the most air the app's neck suggestion puts on an 8 in neck
the most air the app's neck suggestion puts on a 10 in neck

source.section: diffuser selection from the maker's catalogued sound (NC) and throw data, not a code figure

rules.title: Duct gauge by size and pressure class
rules.summary: The simplified gauge schedule the Duct tool picks metal with — by the duct's larger side or diameter and the system's pressure class — before you override it.

values.when: 1 in w.g., larger side up to 12 in
2 in w.g., larger side up to 10 in
3 in w.g., larger side up to 8 in

source.section: HVAC Duct Construction Standards, gauge tables (simplified)

rules.title: Duct Schedule factors
rules.summary: The estimating knobs the Duct Schedule starts with — seam and waste, the quick-bid fitting factor, the design friction rate and velocity cap the ductulator suggests sizes from, and the terminal allowance the static-path check adds at the end of the critical path.

values.when: seam and waste, on the straight-duct pounds
fitting factor, when fittings are not counted individually
design friction rate for size suggestions
terminal allowance (diffuser + flex) added once at the end of the static path

source.section: estimating convention; ASHRAE Fundamentals duct design for the rate and velocity

rules.title: Fire dampers at rated walls
rules.summary: Where a duct passes through a fire-resistance-rated wall, the code wants a listed fire damper at the penetration unless an exception removes it, so each crossing of a rated wall is a damper, an access door and a sleeve on the bid.

values.when: a duct through a fire-resistance-rated wall, a listed fire damper at the penetration, unless an exception of 607.5.2 or 607.5.3 removes it
a grease duct through the same wall (it takes a listed enclosure or wrap instead)

source.section: 607.5 Where required (607.5.1 fire walls, 607.5.2 fire barriers, 607.5.3 fire partitions)

rules.title: Grease duct metal and its weight
rules.summary: A commercial kitchen hood's exhaust duct is welded carbon steel of at least 16 gauge or stainless of at least 18 gauge, never the galvanized gauge schedule, so the Duct tool prices a grease run at that fixed gauge and its own sheet weight.

values.when: cleanout spacing on horizontal duct, at most

source.section: 506.3.1.1 Grease duct materials (NFPA 96 7.5.1 says the same)

rules.title: Make-up air for a kitchen hood
rules.summary: A commercial kitchen hood that exhausts air needs make-up air brought in to replace it, delivered while the hood runs and interlocked with its exhaust fan, so a hood on a plan means a second unit, its duct and its controls on the bid.

values.when: a commercial kitchen hood exhausting air, make-up air to replace it (508.1)
the make-up air unit against the hood's exhaust fan, started and run together (508.1)
make-up air tempered to within a set difference of the room it enters (508.1.1, 10°F in the model code, with exceptions)

source.section: 508.1 Makeup air (interlock) and 508.1.1 Makeup air temperature

amendments.note: Rule 1346.0508 amends the temperature limit to make-up air not less than 50°F at the diffuser.

rules.title: Outdoor air for ventilation
rules.summary: Occupied spaces get a code minimum of outdoor air, set by the kind of room, the people in it and its floor area (a dining room 7.5 CFM a person plus 0.18 a square foot); on a bid the question is whether the plan's supply already carries it or a separate unit does.

values.when: outdoor air to an occupied space, by mechanical or natural ventilation

values.value: per person plus per floor area

values.when: a dining room, per square foot of floor

rules.title: Room airflow by type
rules.summary: The cubic feet per minute per square foot the app assumes for a room type when no target is given — office 1.0, conference and break 1.5, storage 0.5.

rules.title: Galvanized sheet weight by gauge
rules.summary: Pounds per square foot of galvanized steel sheet at each gauge — the basis of every duct weight the schedule reports.

source.section: A653 / A924, nominal galvanized sheet weight by gauge

rules.title: Cleanouts on drainage piping
rules.summary: A drain gets a cleanout wherever a snake has to go in, at the turns of more than 45 degrees, at or just upstream of where the building drain meets the sewer, and at least every 100 feet along a horizontal run.

values.when: horizontal drain, building drain or building sewer, between cleanouts, at most
a change of horizontal direction of more than 45 degrees
the junction of the building drain and the building sewer
values.value: a cleanout at the junction, or within 10 ft of developed length upstream of it

source.section: 708.1 Cleanouts required (708.1.1 horizontal drains, 708.1.3 building drain and sewer junction, 708.1.4 changes of direction)

rules.title: Building drain and sewer capacity in drainage fixture units
rules.summary: How many drainage fixture units a building drain or sewer may carry by size and slope; at 1/8 inch per foot a 3 inch sewer carries 36 and the course's 4 inch carries 180.

values.when: 3 in building drain or sewer, at 1/8 in per foot
3 in building drain or sewer, at 1/4 in per foot
3 in building drain or sewer, at 1/2 in per foot
4 in building drain or sewer, at 1/8 in per foot
4 in building drain or sewer, at 1/4 in per foot
4 in building drain or sewer, at 1/2 in per foot

rules.title: Slope of horizontal drainage pipe
rules.summary: Horizontal waste pipe falls at least 1/4 inch per foot at 2-1/2 inch and smaller, 1/8 inch per foot at 3 to 6 inch, and 1/16 inch per foot at 8 inch and larger, except that pipe upstream of a grease interceptor falls at least 1/4 inch per foot at any size.

values.when: upstream of a grease interceptor, any size

rules.title: Appliance shutoff valves
rules.summary: Every gas appliance has its own shutoff valve, in the same room and within 6 feet of it, upstream of its connector, so one appliance can come off the line without shutting the rest.

values.when: from the appliance it serves, in the same room, at most

rules.title: Gas pipe sizing
rules.summary: Each section of gas pipe is sized for the load it carries downstream, in Btu per hour, over the longest run from the meter to the farthest outlet, so like water it shrinks as it goes.

values.when: what a section of gas pipe is sized by
values.value: the connected load downstream of it

values.when: the length it is sized over (the longest length method)
values.value: the point of delivery (the meter, on the course's job) to the most remote outlet

source.section: 402 Pipe sizing (402.4 sizing methods, 402.4.1 longest length)

rules.title: Grease interceptors
rules.summary: Kitchen, dish and bar fixtures that carry grease drain through a grease interceptor, and the restrooms join the sewer downstream of it, because the interceptor is for grease-laden waste only.

values.when: fixtures and equipment with grease-laden waste in a food preparation area (a restaurant, a kitchen, a bar)
water closets, urinals, lavatories and other fixtures without grease

source.section: 1003.3.1 Grease interceptors and automatic grease removal devices required

rules.title: Hanger spacing for cast-iron pipe
rules.summary: How far apart cast-iron pipe may be supported — 5 feet horizontal (10 feet where 10-foot lengths are installed), 15 feet vertical.

rules.title: Hanger spacing for copper tube
rules.summary: How far apart copper tube may be supported — 6 feet horizontal at 1-1/4 inch and smaller, 10 feet at 1-1/2 inch and larger, 10 feet vertical.

rules.title: Hanger spacing for steel gas pipe
rules.summary: How far apart steel gas pipe may be supported under the fuel gas code, by size, 6 feet at 1/2 inch, 8 feet at 3/4 and 1 inch, 10 feet horizontal at 1-1/4 inch and larger, and vertical pipe at every floor.

values.when: 1-1/4 in and larger steel pipe, horizontal
1-1/4 in and larger steel pipe, vertical

rules.title: Hanger spacing for PEX
rules.summary: How far apart PEX tubing may be supported — 32 inches horizontal at 1 inch and smaller, 48 inches at 1-1/4 inch and larger, 10 feet vertical.

rules.title: Hanger spacing for PVC pipe
rules.summary: How far apart PVC pipe may be supported — 4 feet horizontal, 10 feet vertical.

rules.title: Hanger spacing for steel water and drainage pipe
rules.summary: How far apart steel water and drainage pipe may be supported under the plumbing code, 12 feet horizontal and 15 feet vertical; steel gas pipe hangs closer, under the fuel gas code (plumb.hanger.gas-steel).

rules.title: Gas shutoff tripped by the hood suppression system
rules.summary: When a kitchen hood's fire suppression system discharges, the gas to every appliance under the hood shuts off automatically, and stays off until someone resets it by hand, so the gas line carries a valve the system trips.

values.value: gas to the appliances under the hood shuts off automatically, including an appliance under the hood that needs no protection of its own

rules.title: Indirect waste for food equipment
rules.summary: A sink or machine that handles food drains through an air gap (an air break is allowed for a commercial dishwasher and a pot or dish sink) to a floor sink or other receptor, never straight into the waste pipe, so a sewer backup rises onto the floor and not into the food side.

values.when: food storage, preparation and handling equipment (a prep sink)
a sink that washes, rinses or sanitizes utensils, dishes, pots and pans (a three-compartment pot sink), other than in a dwelling unit
an air gap, above the receptor flood rim, at least

rules.title: Trap arms
rules.summary: How far a fixture's trap may sit from its vent along the drain, by trap size: 5 feet at 1-1/4 inch, 6 feet at 1-1/2 inch, 8 feet at 2 inch, 12 feet at 3 inch, 16 feet at 4 inch.

values.when: 1-1/4 in trap, at 1/4 in per foot, at most
1-1/2 in trap, at 1/4 in per foot, at most
2 in trap, at 1/4 in per foot, at most
3 in trap, at 1/8 in per foot, at most
4 in trap, at 1/8 in per foot, at most

rules.title: Trap seal depth and protection
rules.summary: Every fixture trap holds a water seal 2 to 4 inches deep, and a trap that can dry out, a floor drain that sees no water for months, gets seal protection such as a trap primer.

values.when: an emergency floor drain, or a trap subject to evaporation
values.value: seal protection (a trap primer or a barrier device)

rules.title: Vent terminals
rules.summary: A vent stack ends open above the roof, at a height the adopting jurisdiction sets (the model code leaves it blank), 7 feet up on a roof people use, and clear of air intakes, at least 10 feet away from a door, window or intake unless it rises 3 feet above the top of it.

values.when: above the roof, an unprotected roof extension
values.value: the adopting jurisdiction's figure (the IPC prints a blank for it)

values.when: above a roof used for assembly, a promenade or a deck
horizontally from a door, an openable window or an air intake, at least
above the top of that opening, when closer than the distance above

source.section: 903.1.1 roof extension and 903.1.2 roofs used for recreation or assembly (903.1 in 2018), 903.5 location

rules.title: Venting protects every trap seal
rules.summary: The drainage system carries vent piping that lets air in and out, so no fixture trap sees more than 1 inch of water column of pressure difference and no seal siphons out when the fixture upstream drains.

values.when: pressure difference at a trap seal, at most

rules.title: Minimum water service size
rules.summary: The water service pipe from the main to the building is never smaller than 3/4 inch; the pipes past it are sized to the fixtures they serve.

rules.title: Minimum fixture supply pipe sizes
rules.summary: The smallest pipe that may supply each fixture, 3/8 inch for a lavatory or a tank water closet up to 1 inch for a flush-valve water closet.

rules.title: Inside diameters of water pipe by nominal size
rules.summary: The inside diameter the velocity is computed from, per nominal size, for PEX (SDR 9), copper Type L, CPVC CTS and Schedule 40 galvanized steel.

source.section: F876 (PEX, SDR 9); B88 (copper Type L); D2846 (CPVC CTS, SDR 11); A53 (steel, Schedule 40)

rules.title: Design velocity for water pipe
rules.summary: The velocity the app sizes a water run to, 8 feet per second cold and 5 feet per second hot. Design practice under the IPC, which prints no velocity limit; the UPC caps copper tube at the same figures.

source.section: Plumbing Engineering Design Handbook, Vol. 2, Ch. 5 (cold water) and Ch. 6 (hot water), velocity limits; Copper Development Association, Copper Tube Handbook, "velocity" (5 fps hot, 8 fps cold)

rules.title: Demand curve: fixture units to gallons per minute
rules.summary: The design flow a load of water supply fixture units stands for, in gallons per minute, read off the code's demand table in its flush-tank and flush-valve columns.

rules.title: Water supply fixture units by fixture
rules.summary: The load a fixture puts on the water supply, in water supply fixture units (WSFU), cold and hot, by the private or public column and the kind of supply control.
